**UK fraud losses rise to £1.3 billion as APP scams rebound sharply**

*Authorised push payment fraud reversed its 2024 decline and drove an overall increase in UK fraud losses last year, testing the effectiveness of the mandatory reimbursement regime introduced in October 2024.*

Criminals stole £1.28 billion through fraud in the UK in 2025, a four per cent increase on the prior year, according to UK Finance's annual fraud report published June 15. APP fraud, where victims are manipulated into authorising payments to criminals, rose sharply after falling in 2024, the year the Payment Systems Regulator's mandatory reimbursement framework took effect.

The rebound complicates the narrative around mandatory reimbursement as a deterrent. The framework was designed to shift incentives by making receiving banks share liability, encouraging the industry to invest in prevention. A single year's data does not settle whether the policy is working, but the direction of travel will intensify scrutiny from consumer groups and regulators alike.

For payment service providers, the figures reinforce that fraud prevention is a cost of doing business that is not yet stabilising. Banks and fintechs building detection capabilities, whether through AI or behavioural analytics, will find fresh urgency in these numbers.

*Sources: [APP fraud back on the rise as crooks stole £1.3bn in 2025 - UK Finance](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/47906/app-fraud-back-on-the-rise-as-crooks-stole-13bn-in-2025---uk-finance) — Finextra*

**ACI Worldwide selected to process instant payments for EPI across Europe**

*The European Payments Initiative has chosen ACI Worldwide as its instant payments processing partner, a significant infrastructure decision as EPI scales Wero across the eurozone.*

ACI Worldwide announced on June 15 that it will power instant payments processing for EPI, the bank-backed initiative behind the Wero digital payments wallet. The deal positions ACI as a core infrastructure provider for what is intended to become a pan-European alternative to card scheme dominance at the point of sale and in peer-to-peer transfers.

EPI's choice of processor matters because it signals the initiative is moving from pilot phase into industrial-scale buildout. With the EU Instant Payments Regulation now requiring all eurozone PSPs to support instant credit transfers, EPI needs processing capacity that can handle volume growth across multiple markets simultaneously. ACI's existing footprint in real-time payments infrastructure across several geographies made it a logical candidate.

For the broader market, the deal underscores that instant payments infrastructure is becoming a competitive battleground in its own right. As Wero expands beyond its initial French and German deployments, the processing layer will determine whether EPI can deliver the speed and reliability needed to compete credibly with Visa, Mastercard and established national schemes.

*Sources: [ACI Worldwide and EPI to Power Instant Payments in Europe](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260614185807/en/ACI-Worldwide-and-EPI-to-Power-Instant-Payments-in-Europe) — Business Wire*

**Adyen agrees $335 million acquisition of billing platform Orb**

*Adyen's second major acquisition in months signals a deliberate push beyond payment processing into the broader revenue infrastructure stack.*

Adyen has agreed to acquire Orb, an enterprise billing platform, for $335 million. The deal follows the company's acquisition earlier this year and marks a shift in strategy for a processor that historically favoured organic growth over M&A.

Orb specialises in usage-based and subscription billing for enterprise clients, a segment that has grown as software and platform businesses move away from flat-rate pricing. By integrating billing directly into its payments platform, Adyen can offer merchants a more complete revenue management layer, reducing the need for third-party billing tools that sit between the payment processor and the merchant's finance stack.

The acquisition reflects a pattern visible across the payments industry: processors are moving up the value chain from transaction handling into adjacent financial operations such as billing, reconciliation and treasury management. Adyen's willingness to spend $335 million on a billing platform, after years of minimal acquisition activity, suggests the company sees organic growth in core processing as insufficient to maintain its competitive position against peers making similar moves.

*Sources: [Adyen strikes $335m deal for enterprise billing platform Orb](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/47910/adyen-strikes-335m-deal-for-enterprise-billing-platform-orb) — Finextra*

**UK government proposes open banking as an age verification method for social media**

*The UK's planned ban on social media for under-16s names open banking data as one of several approved age verification mechanisms, opening a new and potentially large-scale use case for account data sharing.*

The UK government is set to announce a ban on social media access for children under 16, with open banking listed among the approved methods for verifying a user's age. Other proposed mechanisms include passport checks, mobile provider data and facial age estimation. The policy, previewed by Prime Minister Keir Starmer ahead of a formal announcement, would require social media platforms to implement at least one approved verification method.

For the open banking sector, this is a notable expansion of scope. Age verification using bank account data would rely on the identity information banks hold on their customers, accessed via existing open banking APIs. It would represent one of the first large-scale non-financial use cases for open banking infrastructure in the UK, moving beyond payments and creditworthiness into identity services.

The practical questions are substantial. Conversion rates, user willingness to share bank data with social media platforms, and the reliability of bank-held age data will all determine whether open banking verification gains traction alongside simpler methods. But the policy signal is clear: government sees open banking rails as general-purpose digital identity infrastructure, not just a payments tool.

*Sources: [UK to unveil under-16 social media ban with face scans](https://www.msn.com/en-gb/news/insight/uk-to-unveil-under-16-social-media-ban-with-face-scans/gm-GMEB320565) — MSN | [Social media ban to be introduced for under 16's](https://aboutmanchester.co.uk/social-media-ban-to-be-introduced-for-under-16s/) — About Manchester*
